content:
As we close 2025 at Form B Design + Research, one moment stands out clearly.

IMTEX 2025.

Not one stall.
Not one machine.

👉 9 of our design projects exhibited across multiple client stalls.

Each one built for a different brand.
Each one solving a different engineering and market problem.
But all carrying the same design intent.

That didn’t happen by chance.
Over the past year, we made deliberate investments:
In marketing (telling our story consistently)
In positioning (design as a strategic lever, not a styling service)
In process (clear phases from concept → engineering → manufacturable reality)
In people and partnerships (working deeply with R&D, engineering, and leadership teams)

And we stayed anchored to
One clear belief:
Industrial design is not how a machine looks.
It’s how a machine performs before it is switched on.

That belief shaped everything:
How we speak to clients
How we structure engagements
How we design machine enclosures, interfaces, and systems
How we balance aesthetics, DFMA, serviceability, safety, and brand presence

IMTEX 2025 was not a marketing milestone for us.
It was a validation milestone.
Validation that:
Design-led machines get noticed
Thoughtful engineering earns trust
Consistent storytelling compounds over time

Most importantly, it reinforced something we’ve believed all along:
👉 When design is treated as strategy, it shows up on the shop floor, on the exhibition floor, and in the market.

Grateful to the clients who trusted the process.
Grateful to the teams who executed under real constraints.
And excited about where this journey is heading next.
Onwards, with clarity, consistency, and conviction.

content:
Machines run on the shop floor, but the people running the business often can't see what they're doing. Gedee Weiler is fixing that with Yantra 24/7, their own CNC machine monitoring software, which they showed on their machines at IMTEX 2025. It gives top management machine data, traceability and the OEE of each machine.

Anjay Goliya of Gedee Weiler said the response was strong, with 80 to 90 percent quality footfall at their stand and one of the best IMTEX editions yet. Good to see an Indian machine builder selling the data along with the machine.
